<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Lands after the open batch (#129 to #137, plus #135's directory edit). Source: governance community/workstreams-audit-2026-11-06.md (Summary and Appendix E) and RULINGS.md C29. Rename forward as C26 did: history, plans 190 to 195, retros, migrations (0031/0032 comments are checksummed), outputs and memory are not rewritten. Step ids (steps, sNN) stay. No store or CLI rename for pij streams. Docs-system writes the schema, docs and skill wording; one coder does the sensor, the claims alias cleanup and any code that reads the folder. Amended 2026-11-08 (pm-001): two phases and two PRs (docs content by docs-system, then rename, code and sensor by a coder), because the rename must ship with the code that reads the folder; templates are v3 because #136 shipped v2 for quoting.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Ruling C29: rename roadmaps forward to workstreams (folder, schema pij/workstream, skill, templates v2, PRD rows), add nesting (part_of), lanes and cross-file ordering, define 'a pij stream is one lane of a workstream', and make coverage a harness checks sensor.

## Non-goals

- Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
- Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
- Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
- One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
